finding.claim: refresh! sends the stored refresh_token and client credentials to a token endpoint of an authorization server discovered from a server-supplied resource_metadata URL, with no binding to the AS that issued the refresh token.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter on a 401 from the MCP endpoint (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:416) and PRM authorization_servers[0] (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:308-327)
finding.sink: POST to token_endpoint with refresh_token, client_id and client_secret (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:661-669, 674-737, 707)

trace.note: parse challenge; resource_metadata taken from header
only HTTPS/loopback check on resource_metadata URL
locate_authorization_server fetches PRM from that URL
PRM authorization_servers entry accepted after HTTPS check only
AS metadata issuer compared only to the same attacker-chosen AS
exchange_refresh_token posts refresh_token to that AS

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS-or-loopback on resource_metadata, AS and endpoints (flow.rb:153-155,237,388-392; discovery.rb:181-194) - does not stop foreign HTTPS hosts. PRM resource must cover MCP URL (flow.rb:513-525) - attacker PRM can satisfy. Issuer equals discovery URL (flow.rb:402-412, 261-262) - attacker AS can satisfy. OAuthURLGuard (http.rb:37-55) covers MCP traffic only, not flow http_client (flow.rb:789-794). No stored AS/token endpoint binding found in provider.rb or storage_backed_provider.rb. Precondition: attacker controls MCP server 401 responses (malicious or compromised server).

finding.claim: A server-supplied resource_metadata URL is fetched unauthenticated with no binding to the MCP origin, including loopback http URLs, letting a malicious server make the client GET hosts on its network.

trace.note: resource_metadata URL placed first in candidate list

finding.guards_checked: secure_url? allows https to any host and loopback http (discovery.rb:181-194, 343-357). Body must parse as JSON object; body not disclosed to caller. No origin or host binding.
finding.repro: Malicious MCP server returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata="http://127.0.0.1:PORT/x"; client issues GET to that loopback service (untested).
finding.trace_note: Impact: blind GET side effects to client-network hosts; no body disclosure.

finding.claim: configure_logging_level writes the server-global logging level, so one session's logging/setLevel changes notifications delivered to other sessions that never set a level.
finding.source: logging/setLevel params[:level] from any connected client (lib/mcp/server.rb:485-486)
finding.sink: server-global @logging_message_notification read by sessions without their own level (lib/mcp/server_session.rb:202-208)

trace.note: fallback to server-global level for sessions without own level

finding.guards_checked: Capability check (server.rb:596-598) and level validation (server.rb:601-603). Per-session storage exists but is bypassed by the global write.

finding.claim: Exception messages from tool handlers and internal errors are returned verbatim in JSON-RPC error data to remote clients.
finding.source: any input that makes a tool handler raise; non-Hash arguments reach arguments.keys (lib/mcp/server.rb:627-630)

trace.note: call_tool wraps exception as Internal error calling tool X: message
generic StandardError path also sends e.message as data

finding.guards_checked: Default exception_reporter is a no-op (configuration.rb:163-165). Generic wrapper at server.rb:507-512 hides messages on non-tool paths only.

finding.claim: A JSON-RPC batch containing a non-object element raises an uncaught TypeError or NoMethodError that terminates the stdio server loop.
finding.sink: request[:id] on a non-Hash element outside the begin/rescue block (lib/mcp/json_rpc_handler.rb:72, 104)

trace.note: batch map calls process_request per element
no rescue around @session.handle_json; only Interrupt rescued at line 55

finding.guards_checked: Streamable HTTP rejects non-Hash bodies (streamable_http_transport.rb:457-459), so HTTP path not affected. Attacker must write to stdin, normally the parent host process.

finding.claim: The authorization response is accepted without an RFC 9207 iss parameter check, a spec-mandated mix-up hardening gap.

trace.note: code and state taken from callback; no iss read

finding.guards_checked: PKCE S256 (flow.rb:369-375; pkce.rb:28-33) and constant-time state comparison (flow.rb:543-550). No grep hit for authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported. Exploit not demonstrated.
